summary: Prepaid reserve not applied after tenant tag truncation during hourly metering run
description: Issue summary: Customer reports prepaid reserved hours (hourly buffer) didn't apply to their finalized invoice for 2026-03-09 hourly window. Impact: customer shows a charge they expected to be offset by prepaid reserve. Environment: prod us-east, enterprise tenant with reserved hours. Observed: postback logs show successful postbacks but ledger did not credit the hourly buffer tag for several keys in the tenant due to tag mismatch caused by truncation in metadata pipeline.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run hourly metering pipeline for tenant BrightAnswers between 2026-03-09T02:00Z-03:00Z
2) Observe postback tags emitted by edge proxies include long org prefix 'brightanswers-enterprise-onboarding-2022-'
3) Postback-normalizer truncates tags >64 chars and drops suffix after 64 chars
4) Billing reconcile expects full tag value 'brightanswers-enterprise-onboarding-2022-xyz' and fails to match, leading to unallocated hourly buffer credit
comments: Support (Aisha): Kunde reports unexpected invoice line for 2026-03-09; flagged to Billing.
Customer (BrightAnswers - Eva Chen): We expected reserved hours to cover the charge; this impacts our month-end budget. Please advise on timing for fix.
Billing Engineer (Luca): Initial hypothesis: tag namespace normalization truncated long tags causing reconciliation mismatch. Gathering postback logs and replaying meter window.
SRE (Marta O'Neill): Confirmed postback-normalizer v1.14 changed truncation behaviour on 2026-03-08; ramping a hotfix to preserve hashed suffix.
Support (Aisha): Applied provisional credit of $1,200 to account while engineering investigates; informed customer of ETA for permanent fix.
investigation_notes: - Identified 9 unallocated postbacks for BrightAnswers during 2026-03-09 hourly window. - The postback-normalizer service introduced string truncation when metadata keys exceeded 64 chars in v1.14 (deployed 2026-03-08). - Billing reconcile joins by full_tag; because normalizer truncated to 64 chars the full_tags didn't match ledger keys created earlier in pipeline. - Reconciliation replay with normalized tags shows credits would have been allocated if the canonicalization matched. - Hypothesis validated by re-running local reconcile job with truncation rule; allocations line up. - Also found one edge case where two distinct long tags truncated to same 64-char prefix, requiring dedup-by-hash to avoid collisions.
resolution: Workaround: provisional credit of $1,200 issued to BrightAnswers on 2026-03-10 and communicated. Permanent fix: rolled postback-normalizer patch (PR #102) that preserves a stable 8-char hash suffix for truncated tags instead of naive truncation; deployed 2026-03-11 at 02:00Z. Ran reconciliation rerun for 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-10 windows and applied retroactive allocations; generated invoice adjustments and credit memo CM-2026-03-135802. Customer notified and credit applied to next billing cycle. Follow-up actions: add unit test coverage for tag canonicalization, add alert for tag-truncation delta >0, update runbook. Linked PRs and runbook created.
follow_up_actions: Add canonicalization unit tests to postback-normalizer (owner: eng-billing)
Add Grafana alert for tag-truncation-rate > 0.1% in hourly windows (owner: SRE)
Run a full backfill reconciliation for past 7 days (owner: billing-team)
Create a Confluence runbook for tag length migration and communicate to Solutions Engineering (owner: DevEx)
customer_communication: 2026-03-10: Acknowledged issue and applied provisional credit of $1,200. ETA for permanent fix 2026-03-11.
2026-03-12: Confirmed permanent fix deployed; retroactive credits applied and credit memo issued. Customer confirmed acceptance; asked for postmortem.
notes: This ticket is related to a broader class of billing mismatches caused by metadata normalization changes; consider audit of recent normalizer releases.
